image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a large marine mammal surfacing in water. The visible portion shows a dark, mottled grey-black skin surface with white patches (likely barnacles or cyamids) near the blowhole area. White foamy water surrounds the lower edge of the animal's back, indicating movement through the surface. The curvature suggests a massive, robust body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a tight crop focusing on the mid-back/dorsal region. The head, rostrum, and specific blowhole structures are outside the frame or obscured by the angle and water spray.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin clearly exhibits the characteristic mottled grey/black coloration with distinct white irregular patches consistent with barnacle/cyamid infestation found on grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible curve of the back is smooth and lacks a true dorsal fin. While the 'knuckles' are not fully resolved due to the crop, the absence of a fin is consistent with the grey whale morphology shown.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The scale of the animal relative to the water displacement and the curvature of the back implies a massive, robust spindle shape typical of large baleen whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed visually; the texture and coloration match the diagnostic description perfectly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth and interior of the whale are not visible in this exterior dorsal shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are located ventrally/laterally and are submerged or out of frame in this dorsal view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail flukes are at the posterior end of the animal and are not included in this cropped image.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The close-up view reveals a non-smooth, textured surface consistent with the rough skin and callosities/barnacles described.

alignment_reasoning: The image strongly aligns with the 'grey whale' class. All testable checkpoints regarding skin texture, coloration (mottled grey/white), and dorsal profile (lack of fin) are met with high fidelity.
